account: It is day 1, about 08:50, and I am in my town hall office for morning business. I read today's appointment book and the addendum and returned all three office books to their chest. My schedule includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen. The addition is an eighteen hundred meeting with the neighbour at town hall, requested during yesterday's tea and accepted by me. The neighbour called it an ordinary meeting; I do not yet know its subject or whether anything is needed. I asked the secretary to check preparations. I briefly saw the neighbour walking near the office this morning, but do not know why they were here. The secretary reports no letters, grain reports, or other business have arrived to her knowledge. Yesterday's accounts recorded my report that the treasury held 128 emeralds, unchanged; no separate account papers or bills had been supplied. There is no clear sign of unusual trouble from what I have seen or heard. For now, the extra evening meeting is the only departure from my written daily schedule, and its purpose remains unconfirmed.
